 Weather Awareness: A Rainy Stretch Ahead for Sonoma
 November 17, 2026 
 By stracy@sonomacity.org 
-->
 Posted on November 17, 2026
 Sonoma is in for a wet few days! The National Weather Service forecasts a storm system arriving Tuesday evening, November 17, bringing periods of moderate to heavy rain, breezy conditions, and a chance of thunderstorms through Thursday, November 19.
 This could be the most substantial rainfall Sonoma has seen so far this season. While some localized ponding and minor drainage issues are possible, there are currently no flood, wind, or cold weather advisories or warnings in effect for Sonoma. 
 What to Expect
 Rain: Rain is expected to begin Tuesday night, becoming steadier Wednesday and continuing into Thursday. The current regional forecast calls for approximately 3.8 inches of rain over the week, with the heaviest rainfall potentially occurring overnight Tuesday into Wednesday.
 Wind: Breezy conditions are expected, with forecast gusts around 20–30 mph.
 Thunderstorms: There is a chance of thunderstorms Wednesday evening into Thursday.
 Road Conditions: Wet and slick roads, puddles, and some localized ponding are possible, particularly in areas where drainage has historically been an issue.
 The City of Sonoma’s Public Works Department, Sonoma Valley Fire District, and other local partners have been coordinating ahead of the approaching storm.
 The good news is that local creeks are still running at relatively low seasonal levels, leaving plenty of capacity for additional rainfall and runoff. Public Works has also been inspecting and maintaining the City’s storm drain system, which is in good condition heading into the rainy season.
 While some familiar trouble spots may experience temporary ponding or minor localized flooding during heavier downpours, widespread flooding is not currently anticipated.
 City crews and emergency response partners will continue monitoring weather and local conditions throughout the week.
 A Good Time to Get Winter Ready
 Our first substantial rains of the season are a great reminder to take a few simple steps around your home:
 Give leaves a little attention. Clear fallen leaves from gutters, downspouts, and drainage areas. Keep leaves and yard debris out of the street, where they can clog storm drains.
 Check around your home. Make sure outdoor furniture, decorations, and other loose items are secure before breezy weather arrives.
 Take it easy on wet roads. Allow extra travel time, watch for standing water, and never drive through flooded roadways.
 Check your supplies. Make sure flashlights, batteries, and other essentials are easy to find in case of a power outage.
 A little preparation now can make the rest of the rainy season easier!
 Sandbags Available for Residents
 For residents in areas that have experienced flooding in the past, free sand and sandbags are available at local self-service filling stations:
 City of Sonoma – Depot Park: 270 First Street West, Sonoma. Free sand is available for City of Sonoma residents. Please bring your own shovel.
 Unincorporated Sonoma County – Felder Road at Arnold Drive: A sandbag filling station is also available at this location for residents in the surrounding unincorporated area.
 Free empty sandbags are also available to City of Sonoma residents at City Hall during regular business hours (up to 10 per resident), while supplies last.
 Residents in flood-prone areas are encouraged to prepare sandbags before heavy rain arrives.
 Reporting Storm-Related Issues
 If you notice a blocked storm drain, fallen branch, or other non-emergency storm-related issue within Sonoma city limits, please contact:
 During business hours (Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.): Public Works Department at 707-938-3332.
 After hours: Sonoma Police Department Non-Emergency Dispatch at 707-996-3601.
 For emergencies posing an immediate threat to life or property: Call 9-1-1.
 Stay Informed and Winter Ready
 Rain is a normal part of Sonoma’s winter season, and a little preparation goes a long way.
 Visit Winter Ready Sonoma for seasonal preparedness tips, sandbag information, emergency contacts, weather resources, and other ways to help your household prepare for whatever winter brings.
 For the latest forecast, visit the National Weather Service Bay Area .
